Subjective: Bryan. Acute low back pain since yesterday. Was raking leaves, felt fine, then ~2h after going inside the back started tightening, with pins and needles in the R foot. Similar episode once ~3 yrs ago, resolved in 1 day. Tried ice and Advil x2 with no relief. Hot shower helped; slightly better sitting. Normally does no physical activity. Partner present, reports pain is worse on standing up. Tingling is in the R leg/foot. No other red-flag questions documented. Meds: none noted besides Advil prn; no prior meloxicam use. Allergies not discussed.
Objective: Pain on lumbar flexion, no pain on extension. Tender to palpation around L5. Dorsiflexion strength normal. Pulses equal in all extremities. Low back x-ray today: normal.
Assessment: 1. Probable lumbar strain/sprain.
Plan: Rest. Meloxicam prescribed (dose not stated in visit). PT referral for stretches and exercises. Patient to message if not improving. Reassess in 2 weeks; MRI if still not improving. Patient and partner asked about an MRI now, and it was deferred. Patient agrees with plan.

additions: Patient has never taken meloxicam before; no prior exposure or known reaction.

Patient does not normally engage in physical activity, and his partner corroborates that he has been sedentary for a long time; physical therapy is intended to improve conditioning, with stretches and exercises.
Patient was advised to send a message if symptoms are not improving, and an MRI will be ordered if pain persists after 2 weeks. The partner asked for an MRI now, but the decision was to wait 2 weeks.
Tingling is localized to the right leg/foot; lumbar flexion produces mild pain, and standing back up from flexion is painless.
